clue.text: Party leads to a long time dressing

parts.note: a band is a group or party of people
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A celebration drags on for ages before anyone gets round to dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads to' simply puts the party first and the long time after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage is a strip of material used as a wound dressing.

clue.text: Spiteful comments about book, reference book

indicators.note: about here means around, so the comments surround the abbreviation

parts.note: bile is bitterness or spiteful talk
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A reviewer writes nasty things about a book that is meant for reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A bible is an authoritative handbook for a subject, as in the gardener's bible.

clue.text: No railway covering the start of route towards the Arctic

indicators.note: covering means lying over and around, so the railway abbreviation wraps the rest

parts.note: taken as written
RLY is the abbreviation for railway
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: There is no train line going anywhere near the route north.
explanation.definitionFit: Northerly means heading north, which is the direction of the Arctic.

clue.text: Using few words in a variety of rich patois

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters appear in another arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone is terse even while speaking a colourful local dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphoristic speech is pithy, packed into short maxims, so it is concise.

clue.text: Just when beginning to adjudicate in points supporting First Lady

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting beneath, so this part comes after the woman

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

parts.note: N and S, compass points north and south

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Just as a dispute about points is to be judged, the President's wife steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's spouse; in crosswords it is usually Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Even as means at the very moment that, just when something else is happening.

clue.text: Recalled story I'd encountered in church music event

indicators.note: the pieces are met inside the church abbreviation, so they sit within it

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the word for story runs backwards

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a tale they came across during a church concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing.

clue.text: Unfortunate account after scoundrel gets American car

indicators.note: after places what precedes it behind the scoundrel word in the answer

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
ill as in ill luck means unfortunate
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A rogue gets a flashy American car, which turns out to be a bad deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadillac is the American luxury car brand owned by General Motors.

clue.text: Plan falling short, keeping fifty out of work

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the shortened word surrounds the numeral
falling short means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A scheme fails, leaving fifty people jobless.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working or unemployed, with nothing to do.

clue.text: Mediterranean locale not initially in a chilly way

indicators.note: not initially means without its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Sicily is the large Italian island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A sunny southern spot is, at first, oddly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Icily means coldly, either in temperature or in an unfriendly manner.

clue.text: Romeo in different items of footwear? That's a lucky thing

indicators.note: in places the radio code letter inside the first item of clothing

parts.note: hose are stockings, one kind of legwear
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a shoe is the other kind of footwear

explanation.surface: A romantic hero wears odd shoes, which might bring him luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different items' asks for two distinct things worn on the feet, hose and shoe, not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

clue.text: Simple dwelling, on reflection, hard to flog

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the dwelling word is read backwards

parts.note: a crib is a humble hut or hovel
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to sell off a basic home after some thought, but it proves a hard sell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like British slang for sell, but here it means to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To birch someone is to beat them with a bundle of birch twigs, a flogging.

clue.text: Airlifted rocks for festival

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Supplies are flown in, perhaps boulders, ready for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid al-Fitr is the Muslim feast marking the end of the Ramadan fast.

clue.text: In a heavenly way energy is brought to article — are you sure?

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
the definite article
'really?' is a way of asking someone whether they are sure

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts a claim that some divine energy is being applied to an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and otherworldly, as if of the heavens, so the adverb describes a celestial manner.

clue.text: Heavily promote, even though lacking in content

indicators.note: with the content gone only the shell is left, so each word keeps just its first and last letters

parts.note: the two ends of this word
the two ends of this word

explanation.surface: A cynic's view of marketing: push something hard even when there is nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two words serve as definition and as wordplay: emptied of their insides they leave the answer. The surface also defines it, since hype is promotion without substance.
explanation.definitionFit: To hype something is to publicise it intensively and often extravagantly.

clue.text: Wretched kid wanting newspaper and a cake

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
taken as written
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A poor child asks for a paper and a bun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy, ragged child.

clue.text: Infatuation about Rector, one in church area

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the infatuation word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a pash is old British slang for a schoolgirl crush
R is the abbreviation for Rector
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crush on the local vicar, felt by one member of the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the district served by its own church and clergy.

clue.text: Pretend there are no problems with father exercising dog?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
PE is physical education, exercise at school
Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: Dad walks the dog and acts as if nothing is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' reads as walking the dog but supplies the school abbreviation for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: To paper over the cracks is to hide difficulties rather than solve them.

clue.text: Right call from muezzin rebounding near the bustling Israeli-Arab city

indicators.note: something that rebounds bounces back the way it came, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
the azan is the Islamic call to prayer given by a muezzin

indicators.note: bustling suggests busy jostling movement, so the little word is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A muezzin's call echoes back across a busy Arab town in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth, in northern Israel, is the country's largest Arab-majority city.

clue.text: Harangue under inverted flag and disappear

inverted means turned upside down, which in a down answer reads it bottom to top

to orate is to speak pompously, to harangue

explanation.surface: A speaker rants beneath an upside-down banner and then vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but it is the verb meaning to lay paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to turn to vapour and vanish, or figuratively to disappear.

clue.text: Disciplinary team I have after opening of prison

indicators.note: after places the team and I have behind the letter from prison
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
a unit is a team or group
I've, the contraction, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A disciplinary squad is installed once the jail opens.
explanation.definitionFit: Punitive means inflicting punishment, which is what disciplinary action does.

clue.text: Equips differently, taking on board extremes of hardy construction

indicators.note: taking something aboard carries it inside, so one piece goes within the other
arranged differently means set out in another order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: extremes are the far ends, so only the first and last letters are used

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone kits out a ship in a new way, loading on board a tough build.
explanation.definitionFit: Physique is a person's bodily build, the way their body is constructed.

clue.text: Woman accepting silver — what's the cost?

definitions.note: the whole question stands for the colloquial 'what's the damage?'

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the woman's title holds the metal inside it

parts.note: a dame is a woman, especially a titled one
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A lady takes some silver and asks what she owes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works only inside the idiom: 'What's the damage?' is a jokey way of asking for the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is informal slang for the price or bill, as in the stock question about what you owe.

clue.text: No source of success in mindlessly following Liberal

indicators.note: no here means without, so a letter is taken away from the phrase that follows

parts.note: slavish means copying or obeying without thought

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician blindly toeing the line never meets with success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party but is the definition; the source of success is removed from the front of the slavish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish and liberal both mean generous or given in abundance.

clue.text: Concert with piano at the end is a lot of fun

indicators.note: the musical abbreviation for soft is shifted from the front of the word to its tail

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: A concert finishing with a piano piece turns out to be great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Piano is P, the music marking for soft; it leaves the front of the concert word and goes to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A romp is a lively, boisterous bit of fun or an easy, enjoyable piece of entertainment.

clue.text: The reverse of drab, I'm one associated with gold

taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.definitionFit: Midas was the mythical king whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Extraordinary restaging of our musical

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

clue.text: Express heading for Swansea at the busiest time

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
peak as in peak hours, the busiest period

explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a train; it is the verb meaning to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak a thought is to express it in words.

clue.text: Bishop, in recess, has pet project

indicators.note: in places the clerical abbreviation inside the word for recess

parts.note: a bay is an alcove or recess

explanation.definitionFit: Someone's baby is informally their own pet project or responsibility, as in 'this scheme is her baby'.

clue.text: Bond's cocktail? Avoid it, kid, not initially shaken

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Advice to a youngster to steer clear of James Bond's drink, not stirred but shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially shaken' looks like a twist on Bond's 'shaken, not stirred', but 'initially' takes the first letters of kid and not.

clue.text: Nag putting space between husband and kiss

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
an en is a printer's unit of space
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: A wife insists on some distance between her husband and a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between' just places the space piece in the middle, after husband and before kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To henpeck is to nag and boss a partner, typically a husband, persistently.
